full_judgment: 10. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that initially the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit land on the basis of settlement but, at the time of hearing the Rule in the High Court Division, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants, giving go by to their claim of title on the basis of settlement, asserted their title in the suit land by way of adverse possession only stating that the plaintiffs' predecessors-in-interest and, thereafter the plaintiffs had been and have been possessing the suit land for more than 90 years. It appears from the schedule to the plaint that the plaintiffs prayed for decree firstly on the basis of the settlement and, thereafter, on adverse possession in respect of 1.383/4 acres of land out of 1.85 acres. Admittedly, the nature of the land is pond. It is case of the plaintiffs that the proforma-defendant Nos.33-62 are the owners of ¼th of the total land. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that there was any metes and bound partition amongst the co-sharers of the disputed land. Since plaintiffs' case is that the defendant Nos.33-62 are the co-sharers of the scheduled tank and banks of the same and that there was no metes and bound partition amongst the co-sharers, it is difficult to accept the submission of Mr AJ Mohammad Ali that the plaintiffs have been exclusively, uninterruptedly and peacefully possessing the suit tank. To establish the plea of adverse possession against a co-owners unambiguous evidence of complete ouster to their knowledge must be established. It is rebuttable presumption that the co-sharers in exclusive possession is holding possession on behalf of the other co-sharers. Possession of one co-owner is in law possession of all the co-sharers. Nothing sought of ouster or something equivalent to ouster will put an end to that possession. In order to establish adverse possession on the part of one of the co-sharer as against another it is not sufficient to show that one of them is in sole possession and enjoyment of the profit of the property. Ouster of the non-possessing co-sharers by co-sharing possession, who claimed his possession to be adverse should be made out. For this there must be evidence of open assertion of hostile title couple with exclusive possession and enjoyment by one co-sharer to the knowledge others. The burden of making out such ouster being on the person claimed into dispute the lawful title of a co-sharer by adverse possession. The concept of adverse possession contemplates a hostile possession i.e. a possession which is expressly or impliedly in denial of the title of the true owner. It is well-recognized proposition of law that mere possession, however, long does not necessarily mean that it is adverse to the true owner. The classical requirements of acquisition of title by adverse possession are that such possession in denial of the true owner's title must be peaceful, open and continuous.
